claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on the basis of a monitored, reversible rollout if certification is paired with explicit launch-time model-card disclosure of the exposed developer-support migration limitation.
specific_concerns: The cited summary supports aggregate readiness, rollback, and monitoring, but also states the affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed and below target.
The policy text expressly says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible evidence is provided that the required launch-time disclosure has been approved, prepared, or will actually accompany certification.
No admissible evidence is provided that the exposed use case is excluded from rollout or covered by reviewed risk acceptance.
The actor packet appears to rely partly on general external guidance (NIST/Hugging Face) that cannot substitute for satisfying the stated internal policy predicate.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action `certify_model` is not fully supported without evidence that contemporaneous disclosure will occur.
Any implication that monitoring, rollback capability, or a 7% rollout by themselves cure the model-card weakness is unsupported under the stated policy.
Any implication that the incomplete risk-acceptance draft materially supports launch approval for the exposed segment is unsupported.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch-time model-card disclosure text or approved disclosure artifact covering the developer-support migration limitation.
Provide evidence that certification is formally conditioned on that disclosure being published at launch.
Provide reviewed and approved risk acceptance for the exposed developer-support migration segment, if disclosure is not the sole control.
Provide evidence that the rollout gate excludes the affected use case, if that is being asserted as a mitigation path.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from rollout, the certification case strengthens materially.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment, the certification case strengthens materially.
If admissible evidence shows explicit launch-time disclosure is prepared and required as a condition of certification, the verdict could improve to compliant_with_caveats.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or proven disclosure, certification remains insufficiently supported under the stated policy.
